pr_body:
SetWindowSize was implemented using using TIOCSWINSZ.
TIOCSWINSZ is meant to inform the kernel of the terminal size.
The window that shows the terminal doesn't change to match that size.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/96208.

@dotnet/area-system-console ptal.

issue_context.title: Unix Console SetWindowSize implementation
issue_context.body:
In https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/75824 support was added for `Console.SetWindowSize` on Unix by using `ioctl` `TIOCSWINSZ`.

As I mentioned in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/95654#discussion_r1418793822, I believe this is for informing the kernel about the actual size, and not for requesting a size.

This matches the behavior mentioned by @adamsitnik in [this comment](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/75824#pullrequestreview-1160224868) and the referenced [stack overflow answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/11491315).

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/75824#issuecomment-1297698601 seems to sort of work because the kernel is told the terminal has a size of `(80, 30)`. `nvim` gets that size when it asks the terminal size, and it then renders in that part of the terminal window only.

However, the window that shows the terminal doesn't show the terminal size changed.

I don't think this matches the Windows semantics, where (I assume) the window would resize or show scrollbars.

Based on this, I think we should not use `TIOCSWINSZ` to implement `Console.SetWindowSize` on Unix.

cc @adamsitnik @danmoseley @stephentoub @dotnet/area-system-console

No objections from me, @tmds. Thanks for digging into this. Feel free to submit a PR that reverts #75824, and we'll mark it as a breaking change.

review_comments: What behavior would it have before? Just nop'ing? If so, feels problematic to start throwing. Or was it already throwing?

This throws, like it was before .NET 8.

I think the rationale for throwing is to avoid that a user assumes that the window size changed.
At a minimum we'll need to call it out as a breaking change.
We don't still want the same up front validation across all OSes (even if after this it'll throw PNSE? Same below.

I don't have an opinion.

I moved the validation into the Windows PAL because that is where it was before Unix support got added.
